Steps to Lodge a Cyber Crime Complaint.
1.Report Immediate Financial Loss: If you have been defrauded of money, call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 immediately. Reporting within the first "Golden Hour" significantly increases the chances of banks freezing the stolen funds.
2.Visit the Official Portal: Go to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.
3.Choose Your Category: Select between "Report Crime Related to Women/Child" (allows anonymous reporting for specific offenses) or "Report Other Cybercrimes" for fraud, hacking, or identity theft.
4.Register and Verify: Create an account by entering your name/email id and a valid Indian mobile number. You must verify your identity using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to your phone.
5.Fill the Complaint Form: Provide accurate details of the incident, including:
Incident Details: Date, time, and the platform where it occurred (e.g., WhatsApp, Instagram, or a specific URL).
6.Evidence: Upload relevant screenshots, transaction receipts, bank statements, or email records.
Suspect Information: Include any known phone numbers, email IDs, or bank account details of the fraudster.
7.Submit and Track: Once submitted, you will receive a Complaint Reference Number. Use this to track the status of your case on the portal.

Anticipatory Bail & Bail Matters in Mumbai – Expert Legal Assistance Before the Bombay High Court and Sessions Courts
When liberty is at stake, timely and expert legal intervention makes all the difference. In Mumbai and across Maharashtra, anticipatory bail and regular bail applications are critical remedies available under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) to protect individuals from unnecessary arrest and prolonged detention.
Our office regularly represents clients before the Bombay High Court, Mumbai Sessions Courts, and Metropolitan Magistrate Courts, providing strategic and result-oriented legal solutions in bail and anticipatory bail matters.
What Is Anticipatory Bail Under Section 482 BNSS?
Anticipatory bail is a pre-arrest legal protection granted under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), corresponding to the erstwhile Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It allows a person to seek bail in anticipation of arrest in a non-bailable offence.

This remedy is especially important where allegations are false, motivated, exaggerated, or where arrest is being used as a coercive measure rather than a necessity.

Courts consider multiple factors while granting anticipatory bail under Section 482 BNSS, including:
	•	Nature and gravity of the offence
	•	Role attributed to the accused
	•	Possibility of misuse of arrest powers
	•	Past criminal antecedents
	•	Cooperation with the investigation
